newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Sept Brent climbing supportive stairway.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Sept Brent climbing supportive stairway.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - JULY 30 -------------
* September Brent continues to hold above trendline support that has been stepping the market higher over the past week, though this support line has been tested every day so far.
* A "contracting triangle" on the September chart moving upward from consolidation on June 20 that ended at $18.70 could tip Brent back to under $17.68 if it completes at $18.70.
Tuesday's bullish API data for U.S crude and gasoline set IPE Brent crude futures above key downtrend resistance and pegged gas oil well above uptrend support, analysts said on Wednesday.
Brent staved off a possible crash as draws in U.S. crude and gasoline stocks took some of the pressure off the market.
On the front month chart Brent closed above trendline resistance from May 16's $20.60 a barrel high after attacking it but dipping to close below it over the previous three trading days.

Independent analyst Elli Gifford said, "Brent has a reasonably neutral structure though it is starting to get a distinctive upward bias with resistance at $18.80, but $18.86 from early July would be a critical break-out point".
However, she said she did not expect the latter level to be broken today with the market starting to look overbought.
September continued to hold above trendline support that has been stepping the market higher over the past week.
This support line has been tested every day so far, but analysts believe that while the prices are on the right side of it the seven week uptrend looks likely to continue.

To the upside analysts said Brent still has some stiff resistance levels to breakdown with the recent high $18.70 on the September chart providing initial resistance, then Fibonacci resistance at $18.80 and key trendline resistance at $19, the high of July 2.
However, slow stochastics are on the point of convergence at a high level and a bear flag forming on the September chart indicate weakness still to come.
Key trendline support is at $18.55-60 today, then $18 and triple bottom $17.90 from June 23-25 bases the market.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International continued to take a bearish tone, "Down now -- To under $17.68 preferably from $18.70 but predicted on $18.79 resistance".
He pointed to a "contracting triangle" on the September chart moving upward from consolidation on June 20 that ended at $18.70.
"This triangle would be eliminated on a print above $18.79 but if the triangle is done at $18.70 the emerging fall should be a five wave affair to under $17.68 lasting more than a week," Graham said.
Gas oil too remains well above trendline support on the daily spot month continuation chart stemming from July 15's low of $160 through $162-$163.25 and coming in today at around $165.75.

Prices made good headway either side of the weekend, peaking at $167.75 on Friday on the back of stronger crude and briefly breaking resistance at $168 a double top from July 3 and July 17 on Monday and Tuesday.
Analysts said the market needs to break above this level more convincingly to go any higher though the 14-day RSI at 59 percent is starting to reach into the over bought zone.
"This market is trying to make a break high but I don't think it will achieve it in the short term," Elli Gifford said.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
